items.stem: Applying De Morgan's law, the expression NOT(A AND B) is equivalent to which of the following?

options.rationale: Correct: De Morgan's law turns a negated AND into an OR of negations.
That is the negation of (A OR B), not of (A AND B).
This drops the negations entirely and is not equivalent.
This is the un-negated original term.

items.stem: Which TWO components are purely combinational, producing outputs that depend only on current inputs? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a multiplexer's output depends only on its current inputs and select lines.

A flip-flop stores state, so its output depends on past inputs.

items.stem: A D flip-flop has a setup time of 2 ns and the data arrives 1.5 ns before the clock edge. What happens?

options.text: A setup-time violation, because data must be stable at least 2 ns before the edge
options.rationale: Correct: 1.5 ns < 2 ns, so the setup requirement is not met.

options.text: Nothing, because 1.5 ns is enough margin
options.rationale: 1.5 ns is less than the required 2 ns setup time.
Hold time concerns stability after the edge, not before.
A violation does not change the clock; it risks metastability.
